quote: Oh, you didn't qualify for it?
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior disqualification she doesn't understand, and the rep's follow-up question goes nowhere useful — he asks which company but drops the actual disqualification reason entirely.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have intentionally avoided digging into the disqualification to prevent surfacing a hard-stop reason before booking, choosing to let the closer handle it instead.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly probe why a prior attempt failed — if it was a hard DQ (roof, credit, ownership) that hasn't changed, the appointment could be dead on arrival and the closer needs that context up front.

quote: Correct? Well, my fiance name is on it. Mine is not at at this time.
stewart_read: The customer discloses she is not on the title — her fiancé is the sole owner — which is a bigger qualification issue than a simple co-owner mention, since the person on the call cannot legally sign for the system.
coaching_implication: Rep should have immediately asked whether the fiancé will be present for the appointment and gotten a direct commitment, not just noted his name for the record.

quote: there is a tax credit in place right now that's gonna be leaving at the end of the year. So, I mean, I'd recommend looking into it as soon as possible just so you can get the ball rolling on it.
stewart_read: Rep uses urgency to counter her 'next year' deferral, which is a reasonable time-anchor move, but he never flips her earlier disqualification confusion or her high bill into an emotional against-the-utility reframe.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as sufficient handling since it did compress her timeline from 'next year' to 'next week,' so the urgency lever worked on its own terms.
coaching_implication: Encourage the rep to pair the urgency lever with the bill-pain reframe once the bill number is captured, rather than relying on urgency alone.

stewart_read: Customer gives a clear, high bill figure. Rep acknowledges it as expensive but does not use it again as leverage for urgency or as the reason to lock the appointment.
coaching_implication: This is the clearest missed flip on the call — the rep should tie the $250-300 bill directly to the appointment ask ('let's get you off that $300 bill onto a fixed lower one') instead of just reacting 'wow.'

quote: Wait. If we were to get a food for it, is this something that can be paid monthly or, upfront complete you know, one the whole thing?
stewart_read: Customer asks a financing-mechanism question that is closer-tier content; the rep answers it directly with a substantive explanation rather than deferring to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's answer is brief and generic enough that it may not have created a real objection, but it still crosses into product/finance territory that belongs to the closer.
coaching_implication: Use the universal escape hatch — 'that's exactly what the specialist walks through on the call' — to keep financing detail with the closer and avoid setting expectations the rep isn't positioned to guarantee.

quote: And then are you gonna are you both gonna be around on Monday next week?
stewart_read: This is the rep's attempt to lock a day, but he gets a hedge in response and does not press for a firm yes/no, alternate day, or specific time before ending the call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to not accept a vague 'I'll let you know' — offer two concrete time windows and ask directly which works, rather than leaving the day itself unconfirmed.

quote: Okay. So we'll just plan on this. Just send me that utility bill as soon as you can.
stewart_read: The call closes with no confirmed date, no confirmed time, and no locked bill-delivery deadline — three separate button-up elements left open.
coaching_implication: This is the compounding effect of the earlier soft scheduling attempts; the manager should walk the rep through button_up's required elements and show how none were locked here.
